title: Model pinning: unified selector resolution, deprecation signals, and rollout/canary playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Establish a single, well-documented pin resolution algorithm across API and SDK clients that supports tag, semver range, and commit-hash pins; define deprecation signals, canary/rollout semantics, and migration guidance for customers and internal ops.
motivation: Customers pin models to ensure deterministic behavior in production. Current behaviour has ambiguous precedence (tags vs semver vs hash) and lacks standardized deprecation/fallback semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. This causes unexpected surprises during rollouts, inconsistent telemetry, and higher support load.
proposal: Define an explicit, simple-to-implement resolution algorithm and SDK surface that: 1) documents resolution precedence, 2) exposes deterministic fallbacks, 3) surfaces deprecation and retirement signals to clients, and 4) supports canary/A-B rollout patterns via pin overrides. Implement server-side audit logs and client warnings for impending deprecations.
resolution-algorithm: 1) Exact hash match (commit SHA/full artifact id) => highest precedence and immutable. 2) Exact semver (e.g. 1.2.3) => matches release artifacts; if multiple artifacts exist for same semver, prefer 'release-stable' artifact with highest stability score; if ambiguity persists, fail fast with descriptive error. 3) Semver range (e.g. ^1.2, ~1.3) => resolve to highest compatible semver that is not marked 'deprecated' unless explicit allow_deprecated flag present in request. 4) Tag (e.g. 'latest', 'canary', 'redwood:beta') => resolve to tag pointer; tags can point to semver or hash. 5) No selector => server default model for customer account and region. Notes: - If resolution points to a deprecated artifact and allow_deprecated is false, resolution should either fallback to a configured pin fallback (customer-level override) or raise a deterministic error. - Resolution must be deterministic for same timestamp and same model registry state; server returns resolved_model_ref and resolved_model_metadata in API response for transparency.
sdk-changes: 1) Add PinSelector type with fields: kind (hash|semver|range|tag), value, allow_deprecated (bool), timeout_ms (int). 2) Expose resolution metadata in response: resolved_model_ref, resolved_from_selector, resolved_timestamp, deprecation_status. 3) Client-side validation helpers to detect ambiguous selectors and recommend explicit hashes for production queues. 4) Warnings emitted via SDK logger when a selector resolves to a tag or semver range in a production environment. 5) New convenience helper for canary rollouts: SDK.applyPinOverride(customer_id, route, pin_selector, start_ts, end_ts, weight) — purely client-side helper that orchestrates calls to rollout API. (Implementation of rollout API covered separately.)
api-examples: 1) Pin by hash: { "model": {"selector":{"kind":"hash","value":"sha256:3a4b..."}} } 2) Pin by semver exact: { "model": {"selector":{"kind":"semver","value":"1.4.2"}} } 3) Pin by semver range but disallow deprecated: { "model":{"selector":{"kind":"range","value":"^1.4.0","allow_deprecated":false}} } 4) Tag pin with expected fallback: { "model":{"selector":{"kind":"tag","value":"canary-us-east","fallback":{"kind":"semver","value":"1.4.0"}}}}
deprecation-policy: - Model artifacts may be annotated with deprecation_date and replacement_hint fields in the model registry. - When deprecation_date is set and within 30 days, SDKs should emit a WARNING. - Within 7 days of deprecation_date, server should reject semver range resolutions that would select the deprecated artifact unless allow_deprecated=true is present on the request. - For hashes, deprecation is informational only (hash pins always win). - Owners can mark 'retired' which will cause resolution to fail and return suggested replacements. - We will publish weekly notices to the Console UI and send tenant-level deprecation events for subscribed customers.
canary-rollout-behavior: - Rollouts are managed via a separate Rollout API but must interoperate with pin resolution: rollout rules can apply pin overrides per route and per weight. - Canary semantics: short-lived tag (e.g. 'canary-2025-02-12') resolves to a specific hash; rollout attaches the tag selector with weight X. - During canary, metric monitoring must compare canary vs baseline for latency, token-cost, and quality (if configured). - If canary fails hard SLOs or triggers quality regression alerts, system auto-triggers failover to baseline pin and records rollback event. - SDKs should provide helper to validate effective pin for a route given active rollout rules.
observability-and-metrics: - Emit resolution events: selector_kind, selector_value, resolved_ref, resolved_kind, resolved_semver, deprecated_flag, resolution_latency_ms. - Track per-tenant counts of non-deterministic resolutions (tag->hash transitions) and warnings emitted. - Add Console dashboard: 'Pins & Rollouts' with active pins, upcoming deprecations, and unresolved ambiguities. - Correlate pin changes with performance profile regressions by tagging eval runs with the resolved_model_ref.
backwards-compatibility: - Default server behavior unchanged for requests without explicit selector. - For existing clients that used 'tag' without allow_deprecated, behavior remains the same but now will start emitting warnings and resolved_model_ref in response. - Add-on: if a legacy SDK relied on implicit fallback to 'latest', document and encourage explicit migration to semver/hash pins for production workloads. - Provide a Transition API mode 'compat' for 3 months which mirrors historical fallbacks; after that period, compat mode will be removed and telemetry will be used to nudge customers.
testing-plan: - Unit tests for resolution permutations: hash->semver->range->tag->default. - Integration tests across hosted/dedicated/private deployments ensuring identical resolved_model_ref for same registry snapshot. - Canary e2e test that simulates a failing canary and verifies automatic rollback. - Load test to ensure resolution adds <5ms median latency to request path. - SDK tests to assert warning emission and metadata presence in responses.
acceptance-criteria: - Implementation returns resolved_model_ref and resolved_from_selector on the API for all selector kinds. - Resolution precedence matches algorithm in this ticket with deterministic output across environments. - SDKs emit deprecation warnings according to policy and expose allow_deprecated flag. - Rollout integration validated with one internal canary run: success path and failure+rollback path both exercised. - Console shows pins & deprecation dashboard with accurate data for test tenant.
outstanding-decisions: - Final naming for SDK PinSelector type (PinSelector vs ModelSelector). - Whether allow_deprecated should default to false at API level or be opt-in via tenant policy. - Exact telemetry sampling rate for resolution events in high-volume tenants. - Format of replacement_hint (free text vs structured model ref).
follow_up-tasks: - Implement server-side resolved_model_ref field and audit log entries (ENG-77655). - Add SDK helpers and deprecation warnings (ENG-77656). - Build Console dashboard widget and deprecation email pipeline (ENG-77657). - Draft customer migration guide and changelog entry for runtime-1.22 (PM/Docs).
